cut_first_review: B00 establishes what audit_review_queue.py is and names its four outputs (beat sheet hash, master probe, frame samples, review leads) and its contract (never approves, never publishes). B01 corrects the core misconception — it documents source structure, it does not decide if a reel ships. B05 introduces the one design insight worth the Short: stale master detection, which names when source and render are out of sync. B07 shows real output from a live run (12 beats, 12 samples, 0 leads) — concrete proof the tool runs. B09 delivers the verdict: stale-master is unique to this tool, 70%-position is a deliberate design choice, and the silent-tile failure is the bite you must count manually. B11 closes with Liam's sign-off. No dangling references: none of the dropped beats are referenced by name in the kept narration. The transition from B01 (misconception) to B05 (design insight) skips the flag walkthrough but the narrative still flows: 'it doesn't approve' → 'here is what makes it useful' → 'here is real proof' → 'here is what bites'. No numbered-list transitions. No repeated conclusions.
